markets.question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
markets.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the named individual wins and accepts the 2028 nomination of the Democratic Party for U.S. president. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of official Democratic Party sources.

Any replacement of the democratic nominee before election day will not change the resolution of the market.

eventMetadata.context_description: The fragmented early field for the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination keeps trader odds tightly clustered, with Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez at 21.1 percent, Gavin Newsom at 15.7 percent, and Jon Ossoff at 13.8 percent reflecting distinct coalition strengths rather than any dominant frontrunner. No candidates have formally declared, so positioning rests on name recognition, fundraising potential, and regional bases ahead of the 2026 midterms. The Democratic National Committee’s approved primary calendar—starting with South Carolina, followed by Nevada, New Hampshire, New Mexico, Michigan, and Virginia—elevates states with sizable Black, Latino, and working-class voting blocs. Recent comments from Ocasio-Cortez on future options and personal timing have sustained visibility, while governors and senators like Newsom and Ossoff draw support from executive records and swing-state experience. Formal announcements, midterm results, and early primary-state polling could create separation before January 2028 contests.
